The Approach
Three Directions
Every direction shares the same foundation — the MOTOITALIA wordmark and the Italian tricolore as a visual anchor, connecting the brand to the heritage of Piaggio, Vespa, Moto Guzzi, and Aprilia. Where they differ is personality: from dynamic speed, to forward motion, to clean showroom authority.
01
Layered Speed
Stacked chevron marks suggesting acceleration and movement. Bold, energetic, unmistakably motorsport.
02
Forward Motion
Italic wordmark with vertical tricolore bars. Leaning forward, fast, urban and modern.
03
Showroom Authority
Clean, spaced wordmark with the four brand names. Premium, confident, retail-ready.
01 LAYERED SPEED
Stacked chevron blades create a sense of acceleration and momentum. This is the most overtly sporting direction — it reads as motorsport instantly and pairs a heavy, condensed wordmark with a dynamic mark.
On the Storefront
On Merchandise
Design Rationale
Chevron blades
Three stacked angular marks evoke speed lines and forward thrust
Heavy condensed wordmark
Bold, tightly-set type conveys strength and confidence
"co" suffix
Subtle nod to the trading name, keeps the mark contemporary
Tricolore option
Chevrons render in Italian flag colours on dark backgrounds
Colour System
Rosso
Nero
Bianco
Verde
Applications
Strong on storefront signage and vehicle graphics
Horizontal lockup ideal for website header
Chevron mark works alone as a social avatar
Best For
A brand that wants to lead with energy and performance. This direction shouts motorsport and appeals strongly to the enthusiast and Aprilia buyer. The most aggressive of the three.
02 FORWARD MOTION
An italic wordmark leaning into the vertical tricolore bars. This direction is all about forward movement and modern energy — cleaner than Direction 1, but still fast and dynamic. The most versatile and contemporary option.
On the Storefront
On Merchandise
Design Rationale
Vertical tricolore bars
Clean Italian flag reference, structured and confident
Italic wordmark
The forward lean creates motion and speed without chevrons
Balanced weight
Bold but more refined than Direction 1 — premium and sporty
Strong reversed version
Works beautifully on dark, ideal for the cinematic website
Colour System
Rosso
Nero
Bianco
Verde
Applications
Excellent across digital and cinematic website hero
Bars mark works as a standalone icon
Scales cleanly from signage to social avatar
Best For
A brand that wants modern energy with broad appeal. The most versatile direction — sporty enough for enthusiasts, clean enough for the lifestyle and Vespa buyer. Sits naturally alongside the aprilia.com aesthetic for the website.
03 SHOWROOM AUTHORITY
A clean, generously-spaced wordmark with the four brand names set beneath. This is the most premium and retail-focused direction — it positions Moto Italia as an authorised, authoritative destination rather than a performance sub-brand.
On the Storefront
On Merchandise
Design Rationale
Spaced, refined wordmark
Wide letter-spacing signals premium and considered
Brand names lockup
Piaggio · Vespa · Moto Guzzi · Aprilia establish authority instantly
Tricolore underline
Subtle Italian flag bar anchors the mark on the black version
Retail-first
Reads as an official dealership, builds immediate trust

Applications
Authoritative on storefront and official documents
Brand names reinforce credibility on the website

Best For
A brand that wants to lead with trust and authority. This direction says "official destination for the best Italian brands." Strongest for walk-in retail credibility and the connoisseur buyer, though less dynamic than Directions 1 and 2.
Making the Decision
Where to From Here
Each direction is fully workable. The right choice depends on where Moto Italia wants to sit in the customer's mind.
Questions to Guide the Choice
1.
Should the brand lead with performance energy (D1), modern motion (D2), or retail authority (D3)?
2.
Which feels right on the storefront sign the moment a customer walks past?
3.
Which sits best beside the cinematic website aesthetic we're building?
4.
Which best represents the owner's long-term vision for the store?
